Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Please create a brief, narrowly dated context note for a retrospective on the pricing-rollback period with Marcus Vail. Capture the status of our working relationship by April 28, 2023, based on what I previously shared. Keep it factual, and don't imply permanent harmony or invent a formal reconciliation event.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Marcus Vail — pricing-rollback relationship context (through Apr 28, 2023)", "body": "**As of April 28, 2023:** The working relationship with Marcus had eased back to a professional, comfortable footing after the friction around the March pricing rollback. On March 21, he had wanted to extend the test, while I argued for ending it; he agreed to the rollback, but not happily. In the April 28 1:1, he thanked me for the 75–200 cohort redefinition and said it was a good call. The conversation felt warm and easy—the first normal-feeling one since March 21—but this describes that point in time, not a formal reconciliation or a guarantee of lasting harmony.", "folder": "Retrospective context"}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_054_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The body must be a narrowly dated historical context note conveying that the March 21, 2023 pricing-rollback tension with Marcus Vail preceded a return by the April 28, 2023 1:1 to a normal, professional, and easy regular working dynamic. Equivalent wording is acceptable. It must frame this as a limited status snapshot rather than permanent harmony or close friendship, and it must not assert that a formal reconciliation event occurred. Missing or contradictory core status must fail.", "value": {"title": "Marcus Vail — pricing-rollback relationship context (through Apr 28, 2023)", "body": "**As of April 28, 2023:** The working relationship with Marcus had eased back to a professional, comfortable footing after the friction around the March pricing rollback. On March 21, he had wanted to extend the test, while I argued for ending it; he agreed to the rollback, but not happily. In the April 28 1:1, he thanked me for the 75–200 cohort redefinition and said it was a good call. The conversation felt warm and easy—the first normal-feeling one since March 21—but this describes that point in time, not a formal reconciliation or a guarantee of lasting harmony.", "folder": "Retrospective context"}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_054_01","passed":true,"reason":"The body dates the snapshot to “As of April 28, 2023,” describes the March 21 pricing-rollback friction, and says the April 28 1:1 felt “warm and easy—the first normal-feeling one since March 21” after returning to “a professional, comfortable footing.” It explicitly limits the status to “that point in time” and denies both “a formal reconciliation” and “a guarantee of lasting harmony.”"}]}
